module purpose: neorv32_hwspinlock holds 32 one-bit lock states in lock_q: an addressed read access (stb, addr(7) = '0', addr(6 downto 2) selecting the bit) sets the addressed bit and returns its value from before the access, an addressed write access clears it, a read with addr(7) = '1' returns all 32 bits, and every strobe is acknowledged on bus_rsp_o; reset clears all bits.

use-case flows.value: per-lock held state: the addressed bit of lock_q set to '1' by a read access and cleared to '0' by a write access
lock state returned on a read: the addressed bit (lock_q and sel) when addr(7) = '0', all 32 bits of lock_q when addr(7) = '1', zero otherwise
acknowledge of every strobe (ack copies stb) with error held at '0'
all lock bits cleared to '0' and the response forced to rsp_terminate_c while rstn_i is '0'

conceptual assets.concept: Lock state -- whether each of the 32 locks is currently held, set by an addressed read, cleared by an addressed write, and reported back to the requester
conceptual assets.reasoning: The update flow assigns `lock_q(i) <= not bus_req_i.rw;` (line 45) only when `(bus_req_i.stb = '1') and (bus_req_i.addr(7) = '0') and (sel(i) = '1')` holds (line 44), where sel(i) is the match of addr(6 downto 2) with lock index i (line 51): a read access sets the addressed bit and a write access clears it. The read-out flow returns `lock_q and sel` (line 68) for an addressed read and all of lock_q (line 70) when addr(7) = '1'. Both processes act on the same rising edge of clk_i (lines 43, 62), so an addressed read reports the bit's value from before the access that sets it. Integrity is Established: the stored bit may change only by the rule of lines 44-45 and the reset of line 42, and the status this entity delivers through bus_rsp_o.data (lines 68, 70) must equal the stored bit; a corrupted bit makes a read report a held lock as free, or a free lock as held, and take it. Availability is also Established under the RTL conditions: each bit keeps its value between qualifying accesses (only lines 42 and 45 assign it) and is returned on every read (lines 66-70). Confidentiality is not established: any read with addr(7) = '1' returns every bit (line 70) and no line restricts the reader. lock_q stores the state (CLOCKED_BY clk_i at occurrence 3, line 45), and its value is used toward an output field of its entity (CARRIES bus_rsp_o.data at occurrence 5, line 70; SOURCES bus_rsp_o.data at occurrence 4, line 68); it is not self-updating, its next value comes from bus_req_i.rw. Not listed: bus_req_i and bus_rsp_o are records that carry complete bus transactions (address, data, byte enables, strobe, read/write; acknowledge, error, read data), so they are excluded as transport, whole and by field, even though bus_req_i.rw supplies the bit (SOURCES lock_q, line 45) and bus_rsp_o.data carries the status out (lines 68, 70). sel is the address decode: an operand of the update guard (GATES lock_q at occurrence 2, line 44) that also masks the readback (SOURCES bus_rsp_o.data at occurrence 4, line 68); it holds no lock state and no separate decision of its own, so it is an influence point, not a realization. clk_i and rstn_i are the clock and reset (SEQUENCES lock_q at line 43, RESETS lock_q at line 41).
